result:
Perfect. The deployment shows the current template has absurd resource requests (**64 CPU, 200Gi memory**), but the `last-applied-configuration` annotation reveals the intended values were reasonable (20m-200m CPU, 48-128Mi memory). I have enough evidence for high confidence.

---

```
ROOT CAUSE: Deployment resource requests were changed to impossibly high values (64 CPU cores, 200Gi memory), making new pods unschedulable.

EVIDENCE:
  - kubectl get pods -n rca-test -o wide -> one pod (demo-app-58cc796977-m8dh9) stuck in Pending state with no node assigned
  - kubectl describe pod demo-app-58cc796977-m8dh9 -> FailedScheduling event: "0/2 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient cpu, 2 Insufficient memory"
  - kubectl describe pod demo-app-58cc796977-m8dh9 -> pod spec shows resources: cpu "64", memory "200Gi" for both requests and limits
  - kubectl get deploy demo-app -o yaml -> deployment template confirms absurd values (cpu: "64", memory: 200Gi) while last-applied-configuration annotation shows intended reasonable values (cpu: "20m"/"200m", memory: "48Mi"/"128Mi")

CONFIDENCE: high

PROPOSED PATCH:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: demo-app
  namespace: rca-test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "20m"
            memory: "48Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "128Mi"
```
